Commentary.Commentary: The first target for New Zealand then is to see off this period till Stumps tonight. The immediate threat will be that of Steyn and Philander and the action will commence soon...

An un-New Zealandish type of effort with the ball and on the field. They were too impatient and let too many loose deliveries and then their fielding did not help either. As many as 4 catches were put down and that did not help their cause. Amidst all this, Neil Wagner bowled his heart out with a 5-fer and was well supported by Trent Boult whose figures do not do him justice.

A fine batting display by the home side. The top 5 crossed the 50-mark and the captain went on to score triple figures. A perfect recipe for a 400-plus or a 500ish total and the Proteas have reached that. They were lucky on the way but won't complain.

56, 82, 58 and 67 not out were the scores of the top four batsmen for South Africa with JP Duminy having a chance to get a big one today. The Kiwis toiled, without much success and it paid on their patience as well, as they started getting inconsistent and tired in the heat. It is an extremely difficult task for a tired bowling unit to come back hard the next day but then that is Test cricket. Will we see a fightback from the Black Caps this morning and keep the Proteas to under 350? Or will the home side maintain their pressure? That ends the action from Day 1 of this second Test. South Africa have been in total command and will look to build on it tomorrow when play resumes at 1330 IST (0800 GMT). Do join us for all the action. Until then, Adios! Take Care!

A tough opening day for the Kiwis. Not much went their way, with the edges going past the fielders, a couple of chances grassed and then, the reviews not being taken at the right time. Everyone tried hard but apart from Boult and Wagner, no one was consistent enough. The latter bowled his heart out with lots of passion and fire and gave the Kiwis something to smile.

Four half centuries by the top four batsmen often sets the tone of an innings and this has not been any different. The only disappointment for South Africa would be that the top three could not go on to get a big one or a century. Still, at 283/3, they are in a comfortable position and will look to get as close as possible to 500 tomorrow.

It was a good start right at the top by a new pair today - Stephen Cook and Quinton de Kock who played confidently and positively, survived a few edges and added 133 for the first wicket. Both were dismissed in quick succession but then Amla and Duminy had a 95-run stand for the third wicket which prevented a Kiwi comeback. If that was not enough, then an unbeaten 37-run stand for the 4th wicket between Duminy and du Plessis has kept the opposition at bay.

South Africa's day, by a long margin. After being put in to bat, they have got close to 300 and lost just 3 wickets. Things might have been different had the catches been held and a couple of reviews been taken at the right time but then that is not South Africa's problem.

OUT! That is as clean as a whistle. No doubts about it. Cook has to go. Fuller and a bit wider outside off, Cook reaches out to drive but the ball moves away a touch and goes off the outside edge. It is towards backward point where Kane Williamson takes it near his ankles. Now, normally, in today's age, when a fielder takes a catch, he shows some emotion - like a fist pump, a send-off celebration, a dance or a jig - but Mr. Williamson, who is as cool as a cucumber, shows no emotion. Just catches it and walks towards his bowler, as if it were a fielding drill. Even Bracewell is confused and does not know what has happened. Cook initially starts to walk but on seeing the bowler, he stops. Now, the umpires get together and have a chat. Amidst all this, Kane Williamson suddenly starts to wonder what is all the fuss? I caught it cleanly, didn't I? he feels. He puts in an appeal and the umpires refer it upstairs. Boy, it is clear from the first replay. Straight into the basket. The decision is made within 30 seconds. Cook departs but he has done his job. A good foundation has been made, albeit, the home side has lost two quick wickets.

To reach this stage after being put in to bat will please any captain and Faf du Plessis is all smiles at the moment. New Zealand have tried hard but they have not been as sharp as they were in the first Test. Join us back at 1040 GMT (1610 IST) to see if they can make any inroads in the second session.

It will be interesting to see how de Kock plays in this role as an opener. He is usually a stroke-maker but this first hour will be critical. South Africa would have thought about Stiaan van Zyl as well, who has opened in the past, but his recent poor returns might have forced them to opt for QdK.

A bright and sunny morning welcomes all of us as the players make their way out to the middle. Stephen Cook and Quinton de Kock are going to open for the Proteas. Tim Southee to start off proceedings to Cook. Here we go...

TEAM NEWS - The Kiwis are unchanged from the previous game. This means that neither of Mark Craig or Ish Sodhi gets a chance. Santner will be the lone spinner. As far as the Proteas are concerned, Dean Elgar is having an ankle sprain. Stiaan van Zyl replaces him. The home side has Dane Piedt as its lone spinner while Duminy can bowl some part-time off spin and van Zyl can bowl some seam-ups.
TOSS - Captain Williamson calls it right this time. After his bowlers' heroics in the first innings of the first Test, he is confident enough to give them a first run. NEW ZEALAND ELECT TO BOWL.

It was a forgettable first Test for both sides as play did not happen after Day 2 at all. A game, played in the early season, did not quite suit South Africa and they were left wondering whether they had done the right thing in scheduling a Test so early. However, the good thing is that the weather is a promising sunny for the second game. Will we see a completed one this time? Hello and a warm welcome to the second Test between South Africa and New Zealand at Centurion.
